name: IN-09
label: Safe R

key_factors: Strong Republican district with a -15 point partisan lean
Incumbent Erin Houchin has a massive fundraising advantage ($1.18M cash vs $18K)
Prediction markets price Houchin at 95% to win
Democratic challenger Brad Meyer has minimal resources and no outside support
model.rationale: The fundamentals point firmly to Houchin: a heavily Republican district, incumbency, and an overwhelming money edge, with markets pricing her near-certain. Meyer's modest fundraising gives no evidence of a competitive race, so the forecast stays close to the fundamentals-based margin.
model.watch: A major late Democratic outside spending surge or a district-wide polling error could narrow the margin, though neither appears likely.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Erin Houchin, the Republican incumbent, is heavily favored to win a second term in this southern Indiana district, which leans Republican by about 15 points. She has raised over $1.8 million and holds more than $1.1 million in cash, while Democratic challenger Brad Meyer has raised about $105,000 with under $20,000 on hand. A Libertarian candidate is on the ballot but has negligible funding.

Prediction markets give Houchin roughly a 95% chance of winning, and no expert raters flag the race as competitive. No public polling is available, so the outlook rests on district fundamentals, incumbency, and the lopsided financial picture, all of which point to a comfortable Republican hold.
